import Mathlib

-- Precondition definition
@[reducible, simp]
def can_jump_precond (nums : List Nat) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  0 < nums.length ∧
  nums.length ≤ 10000 ∧
  (∀ i, i < nums.length → nums.getD i 0 ≤ 10000)
  -- !benchmark @end precond

def is_valid_jump_path (path : List Nat) (nums : List Nat) : Prop :=
  path.length > 0 ∧
  path.head? = some 0 ∧
  path.getLast? = some (nums.length - 1) ∧
  (∀ i, i < path.length → path.getD i 0 < nums.length) ∧
  (∀ i, i < path.length - 1 →
    let u := path.getD i 0
    let v := path.getD (i+1) 0
    u < v ∧ v ≤ u + nums.getD u 0)

-- !benchmark @start auxcode
/-- `PathTo nums path m` is `is_valid_jump_path` phrased with `getD` and with an
arbitrary endpoint `m`; it is the shape that is convenient for induction. -/
def PathTo (nums : List Nat) (path : List Nat) (m : Nat) : Prop :=
  0 < path.length ∧
  path.getD 0 0 = 0 ∧
  path.getD (path.length - 1) 0 = m ∧
  (∀ i, i < path.length → path.getD i 0 < nums.length) ∧
  (∀ i, i < path.length - 1 →
    path.getD i 0 < path.getD (i + 1) 0 ∧
    path.getD (i + 1) 0 ≤ path.getD i 0 + nums.getD (path.getD i 0) 0)
-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definition
def can_jump (nums : List Nat) (h_precond : can_jump_precond nums) : Bool :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  (List.range (nums.length - 1)).all (fun i =>
    (List.range (i + 1)).any (fun j => decide (i < j + nums.getD j 0)))
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition definition
@[reducible, simp]
def can_jump_postcond (nums : List Nat) (result : Bool) (h_precond : can_jump_precond nums) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  (result = true) ↔ ∃ (path : List Nat), is_valid_jump_path path nums
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma
lemma getD_append_lt (l r : List Nat) (i : Nat) (h : i < l.length) :
    (l ++ r).getD i 0 = l.getD i 0 := by
  induction l generalizing i with
  | nil => simp at h
  | cons a t ih =>
    cases i with
    | zero => simp
    | succ k =>
      simp only [List.cons_append, List.getD_cons_succ]
      exact ih k (by simpa using h)

lemma getD_append_end (l : List Nat) (m : Nat) : (l ++ [m]).getD l.length 0 = m := by
  induction l with
  | nil => simp
  | cons a t ih => simpa using ih

lemma head?_eq_getD (l : List Nat) (h : 0 < l.length) : l.head? = some (l.getD 0 0) := by
  cases l with
  | nil => simp at h
  | cons a t => simp

lemma getLast?_eq_getD (l : List Nat) (h : 0 < l.length) :
    l.getLast? = some (l.getD (l.length - 1) 0) := by
  induction l using List.reverseRecOn with
  | nil => simp at h
  | append_singleton xs a ih => simp [getD_append_end]

/-- Extending a path to `j` by one further index `m` reachable from `j`. -/
lemma pathTo_append (nums path : List Nat) (j m : Nat)
    (hp : PathTo nums path j) (h1 : j < m) (h2 : m ≤ j + nums.getD j 0)
    (h3 : m < nums.length) : PathTo nums (path ++ [m]) m := by
  obtain ⟨hL, h0, hlast, hbound, hjump⟩ := hp
  have hlen : (path ++ [m]).length = path.length + 1 := by simp
  refine ⟨by omega, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [getD_append_lt path [m] 0 hL]; exact h0
  · rw [hlen, Nat.add_sub_cancel]; exact getD_append_end path m
  · intro i hi
    rw [hlen] at hi
    rcases Nat.lt_or_ge i path.length with hlt | hge
    · rw [getD_append_lt path [m] i hlt]; exact hbound i hlt
    · have hie : i = path.length := by omega
      subst hie
      rw [getD_append_end]; exact h3
  · intro i hi
    rw [hlen, Nat.add_sub_cancel] at hi
    rcases Nat.lt_or_ge (i + 1) path.length with hlt | hge
    · rw [getD_append_lt path [m] i (by omega), getD_append_lt path [m] (i + 1) hlt]
      exact hjump i (by omega)
    · have hi1 : i + 1 = path.length := by omega
      rw [getD_append_lt path [m] i (by omega), hi1, getD_append_end]
      have hie : i = path.length - 1 := by omega
      rw [hie, hlast]
      exact ⟨h1, h2⟩

/-- The "no cut point" condition implies every index is reachable by an explicit path. -/
lemma reach_path (nums : List Nat)
    (H : ∀ i, i < nums.length - 1 → ∃ j, j ≤ i ∧ i < j + nums.getD j 0) :
    ∀ m, m < nums.length → ∃ path, PathTo nums path m := by
  intro m
  induction m using Nat.strong_induction_on with
  | _ m ih =>
    intro hm
    cases m with
    | zero =>
      refine ⟨[0], ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
      · simp
      · simp
      · simp
      · intro i hi
        simp only [List.length_cons, List.length_nil] at hi
        have : i = 0 := by omega
        subst this
        simpa using hm
      · intro i hi
        simp at hi
    | succ m' =>
      obtain ⟨j, hj1, hj2⟩ := H m' (by omega)
      obtain ⟨path, hp⟩ := ih j (by omega) (by omega)
      exact ⟨path ++ [m' + 1],
        pathTo_append nums path j (m' + 1) hp (by omega) (by omega) hm⟩

/-- A valid path forces the "no cut point" condition. -/
lemma path_to_greedy (nums path : List Nat) (h : is_valid_jump_path path nums) :
    ∀ i, i < nums.length - 1 → ∃ j, j ≤ i ∧ i < j + nums.getD j 0 := by
  obtain ⟨hL, hhead, hlast, hbound, hjump⟩ := h
  rw [head?_eq_getD path hL] at hhead
  rw [getLast?_eq_getD path hL] at hlast
  have h0 : path.getD 0 0 = 0 := by simpa using hhead
  have hlst : path.getD (path.length - 1) 0 = nums.length - 1 := by simpa using hlast
  intro i hi
  have hex : ∃ k, k < path.length ∧ i < path.getD k 0 :=
    ⟨path.length - 1, by omega, by rw [hlst]; omega⟩
  obtain ⟨k, hk1, hk2, hmin⟩ :
      ∃ k, k < path.length ∧ i < path.getD k 0 ∧
        ∀ k' < k, ¬(k' < path.length ∧ i < path.getD k' 0) := by
    refine ⟨Nat.find hex, (Nat.find_spec hex).1, (Nat.find_spec hex).2, ?_⟩
    intro k' hk'
    exact Nat.find_min hex hk'
  have hk0 : k ≠ 0 := by
    intro hc
    subst hc
    rw [h0] at hk2
    omega
  obtain ⟨k', rfl⟩ : ∃ k', k = k' + 1 := ⟨k - 1, by omega⟩
  have hnot := hmin k' (by omega)
  have hle : path.getD k' 0 ≤ i := by
    by_contra hcon
    exact hnot ⟨by omega, by omega⟩
  obtain ⟨ha, hb⟩ := hjump k' (by omega)
  exact ⟨path.getD k' 0, hle, by omega⟩

lemma can_jump_eq (nums : List Nat) (h : can_jump_precond nums) :
    can_jump nums h = true ↔
      ∀ i, i < nums.length - 1 → ∃ j, j ≤ i ∧ i < j + nums.getD j 0 := by
  simp only [can_jump, List.all_eq_true, List.any_eq_true, List.mem_range, decide_eq_true_eq]
  constructor
  · intro h1 i hi
    obtain ⟨j, hj1, hj2⟩ := h1 i hi
    exact ⟨j, by omega, hj2⟩
  · intro h1 i hi
    obtain ⟨j, hj1, hj2⟩ := h1 i hi
    exact ⟨j, by omega, hj2⟩
-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem can_jump_postcond_satisfied (nums : List Nat) (h_precond : can_jump_precond nums) :
    can_jump_postcond nums (can_jump nums h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  have hn : 0 < nums.length := h_precond.1
  constructor
  · intro h
    have H := (can_jump_eq nums h_precond).mp h
    obtain ⟨path, hL, h0, hlast, hbound, hjump⟩ := reach_path nums H (nums.length - 1) (by omega)
    refine ⟨path, hL, ?_, ?_, hbound, ?_⟩
    · rw [head?_eq_getD path hL, h0]
    · rw [getLast?_eq_getD path hL, hlast]
    · intro i hi
      exact hjump i hi
  · rintro ⟨path, hpath⟩
    exact (can_jump_eq nums h_precond).mpr (path_to_greedy nums path hpath)
  -- !benchmark @end proof

## What I did

**Implementation** (`code` section) — `can_jump` decides the cut-point characterization directly:

```lean
(List.range (nums.length - 1)).all (fun i =>
  (List.range (i + 1)).any (fun j => decide (i < j + nums.getD j 0)))
```

i.e. *for every `i < n-1` some `j ≤ i` jumps strictly past `i`*. This is O(n²) rather than the O(n) greedy scan, but it is executable, total, and is exactly the predicate the proof needs — no auxiliary invariant about a running maximum.

**Proof structure:**

| Piece | Role |
|---|---|
| `PathTo` (auxcode) | `is_valid_jump_path` restated with `getD` and a free endpoint `m` — the induction-friendly form |
| `getD_append_lt`, `getD_append_end` | indexing into `path ++ [m]`, proved by list induction so they don't depend on fragile library names |
| `head?_eq_getD`, `getLast?_eq_getD` | bridge `head?`/`getLast?` in the spec to `getD` |
| `pathTo_append` | extend a path ending at `j` by one index `m` with `j < m ≤ j + nums[j]` |
| `reach_path` | strong induction on `m`: every `m < n` has an explicit witness path |
| `path_to_greedy` | converse — `Nat.find` picks the *first* path entry exceeding `i`; its predecessor `u ≤ i` satisfies `i < path[k] ≤ u + nums[u]` |
| `can_jump_eq` | `can_jump = true ↔` the cut-point condition (`all`/`any` unfolding) |

The final theorem chains these: forward gives a path for endpoint `n - 1` (using `0 < nums.length` from the precondition to justify `n - 1 < n`), backward feeds any valid path into `path_to_greedy`.

No `sorry`, `axiom`, `partial`, or other escape hatches; only `Solution.lean` was modified, within the four marker regions.
